description: Every physiological parameter of the generic adaptive cell and its cell types, with its source. The builder (tools/build_adaptive_cell.py) reads this file and writes the module and supermodule instance CSVs: a value taken from here keeps this source in the CSV; values the builder derives (calibrations to the resting state) are marked calibrated there, with the inputs named. status: sourced (a cited value), placeholder (needs a source), design (a chosen operating point), definitional (a definition or physical constant), set (carried over from another module of the library).
source_keys: bib keys in each module version's references.bib; "uniprot" = UniProt entries named in the note; "unreferenced_placeholder" = no source yet.

R.note: gas constant, as the library's SN modules

F.note: Faraday constant, as the library's SN modules

c_std.note: standard concentration 1 M for thermodynamic factors

dT_Q10.note: definition of Q10 (rate ratio per 10 K)

H_ref.note: pH 7: sets the scale of the lactic-acid activity only

T.note: operating point 20 C, the temperature Lynch & Marinov normalise maintenance costs to

R_cell.note: a 2 um cell (typical prokaryote): disc radius

h_cell.note: depth of the 2D sheet, equal to the cell diameter

c_m.note: specific membrane capacitance about 0.9 uF/cm2; 1 is conventional

maintenance_coefficient.note: C_M = 0.39 V^0.88 x 1e9 ATP/cell/h at 20 C (V in um3): the coefficient, ATP/h

maintenance_exponent.note: exponent of cell volume in the maintenance cost

growth_cost_coefficient.note: growth cost C_G = 26.6e9 V^0.97 ATP per cell (check against the itemised daughter cost only)

growth_cost_exponent.note: exponent of cell volume in the growth cost

V_rest.note: BNID 103386: E. coli membrane potential -140 to -105 mV, fermenting at the less negative end

Nai.note: cytosolic Na+ in a marine prokaryote

Ki.note: BNID 107114: E. coli cytosolic K+ 180-200 mM

Cai.note: free cytosolic Ca2+ in E. coli 90 +- 10 nM

pH_o.note: Proterozoic sea, between the early Archean 6.5-7.0 and the Phanerozoic 7.5-9.0

ATP.note: glucose-fed, exponentially growing E. coli: ATP 9.6 mM

ADP.note: ADP of order 0.5 mM in E. coli (about 0.56 mM by Bennett et al. 2009; to confirm)

Pi.note: cytoplasmic Pi kept near 10 mM by the Pho regulon (1-10 mM reported)

glc_e.note: glucose in the medium between food: a lean background, 0.1 mM (open-ocean dissolved glucose is nM-uM; placeholder). The cell is calibrated to just maintain itself here, so growth needs food

glc_i.note: glucose inside an uptake-limited cell at rest: low, so glycolysis has ~50x headroom (growing fermenters run 10-40x their maintenance flux)

H_ATPase_share.note: share of the resting ATP turnover spent by the F1Fo H+-ATPase

NhaA_share.note: share of the pumped H+ returning through NhaA

KefC_share.note: share of the pumped H+ returning through KefC (the rest: the H+ leak)

NCX_share.note: Na/Ca exchanger cycles per NhaA cycle

NaK_share.note: Na+/K+-ATPase share of the ATP turnover in mammals, 19-28% (for the eukaryotic pump module)

V_NaK.note: operating point of the eukaryotic Na/K pump module's own instance

beta_H.note: E. coli cytoplasmic buffering about 50 mM per pH unit

n_H.note: E. coli c10 ring over 3 catalytic sites: 10/3 H+ per ATP

r_H_ATPase.note: ATP hydrolysed per H+-ATPase per second at full activity (order 100)

K_m_ATP_H.note: H+-ATPase affinity for ATP, order 0.1-0.5 mM

pH_act_H_ATPase.note: H+-ATPase half-activated at pH 7.6: regulates cytoplasmic pH at 7.6-7.8, more active as the cytoplasm acidifies

dG0_ferm.note: textbook standard Gibbs energy of glucose -> 2 lactate (BioNumbers BNID 106539 lists -183.6 kJ/mol)

dG0_hyd.note: textbook standard Gibbs energy of ATP hydrolysis

dG0_store.note: glucose + 2 ATP -> glycogen unit: textbook steps via G6P, G1P, UDP-glucose with PPi hydrolysis

h_lac_gly.note: glucose to lactate in bicarbonate buffer: 63 kJ released per mol lactate

h_ATP.note: enthalpy of ATP hydrolysis -20.5 kJ/mol at 25 C

h_glyc_poly.note: enthalpy of adding a glucose to glycogen, taken as zero

K_glc.note: lumped glycolysis affinity for glucose (glucokinase order 0.1 mM)

K_lac.note: lumped glycolysis product constant for lactate

K_ATP_gly.note: lumped glycolysis product constant for ATP

K_ADP_hyd.note: maintenance ATPase product constant for ADP

K_Pi_hyd.note: maintenance ATPase product constant for Pi

glycogen_store_rate.note: storage capacity at full allocation, as a multiple of the resting glycolytic flux

glycogen_mobilise_rate.note: mobilisation capacity, as a multiple of the resting glycolytic flux

K_ATP_store.note: ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase ATP affinity, order 1 mM

C_glyc_max.note: glycogen ceiling: about 10% of dry weight (cell 1.1 g/mL, 30% dry), in mM glucose units

K_Pi_mob.note: phosphorylase affinity for Pi, order 5 mM

K_i_ATP_mob.note: ATP inhibits mobilisation, so glycogen is spent when ATP falls

K_glc_t.note: Glf glucose facilitator of Zymomonas mobilis, Km 4.1 mM

K_lac_t.note: lactate-/H+ symporter affinity for lactic-acid activity (no prokaryotic exporter characterised here)

lactate_exporter_headroom.note: exporter capacity / resting lactate flux, so export keeps up with growth at ~50x the resting flux

gamma_Ca.note: single-channel conductance of a Ca leak pathway

K_m_ATP_NaK.note: Na/K pump affinity for ATP, order 0.1-0.5 mM

B_Ca_total.note: the SN soma's fixed buffer (matveev2002new); bacterial Ca buffering not characterised here

k_bind_Ca.note: the SN soma's buffer on-rate (matveev2002new, quoted set)

k_unbind_Ca.note: the SN soma's buffer off-rate (matveev2002new, actual set)

c_syn.note: ~P per amino acid made from glucose; Akashi & Gojobori give 12-74, 24 assumed as the proteome mean

c_poly.note: textbook: 2 ~P to charge the tRNA (ATP -> AMP) and 2 GTP for elongation

c_deg.note: ClpXP-type proteolysis about 1 ATP per residue translocated (reported 0.15-1)

c_recycle.note: 0.25-1 ATP per amino acid recycled (Lynch & Marinov 2015 supplement)

k_deg.note: BNID 109924: bulk protein degradation about 1%/h in E. coli

K_m_ATP_prot.note: ribosome and synthetase ATP affinity, order 0.1 mM

L_proteome.note: mean protein length about 300 amino acids

glycolytic_share.note: glycolytic enzymes as a share of the proteome

L_glycolytic.note: mean length of the glycolytic enzymes

L_H_ATPase.note: E. coli F1Fo: alpha3 beta3 gamma delta epsilon a b2 c10 (UniProt P0ABB0, P0ABB4, P0ABA6, P0ABA4, P0A6E6, P0AB98, P0ABA0, P68699)

L_LacT.note: E. coli LldP as the size of a lactate carrier (UniProt P33231)

turnover_NhaA.note: transport cycles per NhaA copy per second at rest or capacity: sets its copy number

turnover_KefC.note: transport cycles per KefC copy per second at rest or capacity: sets its copy number

turnover_Trk.note: transport cycles per Trk copy per second at rest or capacity: sets its copy number

turnover_Glf.note: transport cycles per Glf copy per second at rest or capacity: sets its copy number

turnover_LacT.note: transport cycles per LacT copy per second at rest or capacity: sets its copy number

footprint_H_ATPase.note: membrane area one H_ATPase copy takes (0: cytosolic)

footprint_NhaA.note: membrane area one NhaA copy takes (0: cytosolic)

footprint_KefC.note: membrane area one KefC copy takes (0: cytosolic)

footprint_Trk.note: membrane area one Trk copy takes (0: cytosolic)

footprint_NCX.note: membrane area one NCX copy takes (0: cytosolic)

footprint_Glf.note: membrane area one Glf copy takes (0: cytosolic)

footprint_LacT.note: membrane area one LacT copy takes (0: cytosolic)

footprint_Glyc.note: membrane area one Glyc copy takes (0: cytosolic)

footprint_proteome.note: membrane area one proteome copy takes (0: cytosolic)

protein_area_max_fraction.note: most of the cell surface the adaptable proteins may take (placeholder; membrane proteins cover 30-50% of a bacterial membrane, transporters part of that)

tau_expression.note: time constant with which expression approaches its target (user decision 2026-10-08)

build_capacity.note: most ATP one protein's synthesis can take, as a multiple of the resting ATP turnover

build_ATP_floor.note: ATP at which building protein and growth stop (stringent response); full speed at the resting ATP

mRNA_per_um3.note: about 1,380 mRNAs in an E. coli cell of about 1 um3 (BioNumbers)

t_half_mRNA.note: 80% of E. coli mRNA half-lives 3-8 min (median ~5 min)

ribosomes_per_um3.note: 7,000-70,000 ribosomes per E. coli cell with growth rate; the slow end per um3

k_ribo.note: rRNA is stable in growing cells; 1%/h

c_nt_denovo.note: of order 50 ~P per nucleotide made from glucose

c_lipid.note: two C16 acyl chains (ATP and NADPH counted as ~P) plus head group: ~100 ~P per phospholipid

genome_nt.note: an E. coli-sized genome, 4.6 Mb, both strands

K_m_ATP_bio.note: polymerase and synthetase ATP affinity, order 0.1 mM

damage_lifetime.note: an unrepaired cell accumulates a lethal load in 10 days at 20 C

repair_capacity_ratio.note: full repair removes damage up to 10x as fast as it accrues

K_D.note: repair is half-maximal at a tenth of a lethal load

repair_cost_fraction.note: repairing a whole lethal load costs 10% of building a daughter

L_Flagellum.note: one flagellum: ~20,000 flagellin (FliC, 498 aa) in the filament, ~120 hook FlgE (402 aa) and ~300 basal-body, rotor and stator proteins (~400 aa each)

footprint_Flagellum.note: membrane area of a basal body (~45 nm ring) with its stators

n_H_rev.note: about 1,200 H+ per revolution of the E. coli/Streptococcus flagellar motor

f_flag_ref.note: flagellar rotation at the resting proton motive force: ~100 Hz in swimming E. coli (motor speed is proportional to the PMF)

v_swim_one.note: swimming speed with one flagellum turning at f_flag_ref (E. coli with 4-6 flagella swims 20-30 um/s)

flagella_half.note: flagella at which extra flagella add half as much again: speed saturates with the number (thrust and drag both grow)

n_flagella_init.note: the starting cell has one flagellum (user decision 2026-10-09)

eta_water.note: dynamic viscosity of seawater at 20 C and 35 g/kg salinity, about 1.08 mPa s (Sharqawy et al. 2010 tables; to cite)

tau_bundle.note: time for the flagella to spin up into a bundle when the motors switch on, or to unwind when they stop (E. coli bundles form in a few tenths of a second; Turner, Ryu and Berg 2000, to cite): thrust follows the motor switch with this time constant
